BBC News — published 2026-09-29T09:10:03Z, confirmed from article metadata. Search highlights. NOTE: this is PRE-speech (Tuesday morning).
"Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss"
SHARON GRAHAM, general secretary, Unite, to BBC Radio 4 Today: "Instead of going to try and pick the pocket of pensioners, we need to move over to the other side of the equation and think about things like wealth taxes way before we try to stop something like the triple lock." "Going to a group of people who are getting around £12,500 a year in order to pay for it [social care], to take away their security, is wrong - I think its morally wrong." She highlighted that current UK pensions are the lowest of the G7 countries and warned of repeating the unpopular removal of the Winter Fuel Allowance under Starmer.
LUCY POWELL, deputy leader and Education Secretary, Tuesday morning: "I can absolutely assure your viewers watching this that we are committed to the triple lock, it's in our manifesto. The triple lock is really delivering for pensioners right now: [over this] parliament it's set to increase ... by around about £2,000 ..."
ALAN MILBURN, former Labour minister leading an independent review into young people and work, on the BBC's Political Thinking podcast, asked if social care could be funded by getting rid of the triple lock: Burnham was "exactly the sort of person who can take the big decisions". "Andy is absolutely right about this - the social care system is broken... That is going to be a really big call. But it's the sort of call that I've got no doubt - from everything, and every conversation I've been in with him - it's the sort of call that he is prepared to make."
